newsitem.title: REPUBLIC OF IRELAND: Horse Racing-Ireland's Danoli runs at Fairyhouse.
newsitem.headline: Horse Racing-Ireland's Danoli runs at Fairyhouse.

text.p: Ireland's equine star Danoli will run in Sunday's Grade One Drinmore Novice Chase at Fairyhouse, County Meath, trainer Tom Foley said on Friday.
Foley said the gelding will be ridden by Tommy Treacy.
"At the present time there is no reason why Danoli won't run," the Bagenalstown, County Carlow, handler said.
"But it's still a long way to Sunday. All he has to do is get caste in his box, pull a muscle, maybe go off his feed. There is an awful lot of things that could go wrong," he added.
Danoli is likely to face stiff competition in Sunday's two miles and four furlongs (4-km) race from eight opponents.

Amongst his rivals will be the Michael Hourigan-trained Doran's Pride and the British entry, Paul Nicholls-trained See Doran's Pride, winner of the Stayers Hurdle at Cheltenham in 1995, has impressed in winning both of his two chases, at Limerick and Punchestown, County Kildare, this season.
He will be ridden by Richard Dunwoody on Sunday.
See More Business will be ridden by Antrim-born Tony McCoy who was champion national hunt jockey in Britain last season.
McCoy, 22, etched his name in British jump racing's record books earlier this month when he completed the fastest century of winners.
See More Business made a successful return to racing after a long lay-off when winning impressively at Chepstow three weeks ago on his debut over fences.
Danoli first caught the imagination of the racing public in 1994 when he landed the top novice hurdle race at the Cheltenham Festival of racing and another top hurdle race at Aintree.
This season he has reverted to chasing and he is unbeaten in two outings.
He won on his chasing debut at Clonmel, County Tipperary, on November 1 and followed this up with a win over fences in Naas, County Kildare, eight days later.
"Danoli, perhaps, won't be at his best until after Christmas but he could possibly run a good respectable race on Sunday. We'd be disappointed if he got beaten," Foley said.
"But they are big fences at Fairyhouse. They will take a good bit of jumping and a lot will depend on the way he jumps," he added.
The fact that the ground at Fairyhouse is likely to be on the soft side on Sunday after the rain that fell in Ireland over the past week does not bother Foley.
"I'd prefer to see it that way. His shins were a bit sore at Naas last time out and it might suit us that bit better to have cut in the ground," the trainer said.
There are three Grade One races on Sunday's card for Fairyhouse, an indication that the build-up to the 1997 Cheltenham Festival of Racing is well underway.
